profile.reading:
Per Vantage Data Centers' own press release, this building, VA12, sits on the Ashburn I campus at 45200 Vantage Data Plaza, Sterling, VA 20166. Vantage states VA12 reaches more than 250,000 square feet at full completion, with Phase 1 delivering 16 megawatts of critical IT load and the full build reaching 32 megawatts; Phase 1 came online April 28, 2021, brought online in what Vantage describes as just 10 months. The release also highlights an on-site solar and wind installation Vantage calls the first of its kind in Northern Virginia. At the time of VA12's opening, Vantage described the campus as a 146-megawatt, 42-acre "mega campus" with five facilities planned; the campus has since grown, with Vantage's current page describing Ashburn I as 52 acres, six data centers, 1.7 million square feet at full buildout, and 206 megawatts total.

Vantage is a private, Denver, Colorado-headquartered operator; DigitalBridge acquired the company in March 2017, and in January 2024 Vantage announced a $6.4 billion equity investment round led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake. Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility: in November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates raising a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 data center rate class effective January 1, 2027, per Inside Climate News.

Northern Virginia's Loudoun and Prince William counties together form the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and local zoning debate has intensified as residents, county supervisors, and Dominion Energy weigh the tradeoff between substantial commercial tax revenue from facilities like this one and rising transmission-line construction, land consumption, and residential electricity-rate pressure tied to data center growth. Dominion Energy's long-range integrated resource plans have repeatedly cited this region's data center demand as the single largest driver of the utility's near-term generation and transmission capital spending, a dynamic that has also drawn scrutiny from the Virginia State Corporation Commission in periodic rate cases. Vantage's Virginia cluster sits among the densest concentration of competing operators anywhere in the world, including Amazon Web Services, Equinix, Digital Realty, and QTS facilities within a few miles.

reading.body:
Vantage VA12 is one building in the Ashburn I campus, a six-building site in Sterling, Virginia that the operator describes as totaling 206 MW of critical IT load and 1.7 million square feet at full buildout, with over one million square feet already operational. The operator publishes densities up to 300 watts per square foot across the campus. No individual building-specific power figure has been published for VA12 itself.

At the campus-wide 206 MW figure and typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, Ashburn I could house roughly 5,000 racks when fully built. The campus sits in Virginia, which has 1,375 MW of published data center capacity across 23 facilities with disclosed power specs out of 326 mapped sites in the state. Ashburn I ranks 24th in published capacity within the state, meaning this single campus has less capacity than the top 23 individual published facilities.

The Vantage facility is wired for high power density, which qualifies it to host large accelerator clusters. The buildout timeline and operational status of individual buildings remain unpublished.
